title: Laredo ISD Police Hold First Donut Dash 5K, Trading Toys for Miles to Brighten Christmas for Local Kids

content:
The Laredo ISD Police Department held its first Donut Dash 5K on Saturday, Nov. 21, turning a morning run into a toy drive for local children — no cash entry, just a new toy and a pair of running shoes.

Runners and walkers gathered at the Shirley Field parking lot, with check-in at 7 a.m. and the race starting at 8 a.m. Instead of a registration fee, organizers asked each participant to bring one new toy valued at $25 or more. The donations benefit children ages 5 to 18, both boys and girls.

LISD Police Chief Doreen Hale said the event stayed true to its name. “Absolutely, there will be donuts involved. For anybody that wants one, and as soon as they finish the run, the donuts will be there for them,” Hale told KGNS. She added that participants could take part at their own pace: “You can walk, run, crawl, whatever you want to do, we’ll be there for you.”

Part of a bigger holiday effort

The Donut Dash feeds into the department’s “Feliz Navidad Christmas Express,” an initiative in which officers deliver toys to children during the Christmas season. The 5K is the department’s newest way to stock that effort — and to get the community moving together for a cause.

The department has not yet announced how many toys Saturday’s run collected. The toys gathered will go to children across the Laredo ISD community in the weeks leading up to Christmas.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026; Laredo ISD, Nov. 2026.
